term: historical reliabilism and externalist epistemic status in Goldman 1979
definition: An actual belief’s justificational status depends on its suitable cognitive ancestry rather than solely on the subject’s present ability to supply reasons. Principles (6A)–(6B) distinguish belief-independent reliable generation and belief-dependent conditionally reliable operations on justified inputs, with a proposed closure clause. The paper later qualifies this initial account.
note: Source-specific positive proposal, not a definition of all epistemic warrant or an established norm. Its proposed foundational base is not arbitrary concession; its independent adequacy remains disputed. Externalist is the comparison label for denial of mandatory privileged epistemic access, not an attribution of processes necessarily external to the organism or a claim that Goldman uses that label here.
